channel.title: Priceline Pharmacy Pacific Fair – Health advice
channel.description: Pharmacist-reviewed health, skincare and wellbeing advice from Priceline Pharmacy Pacific Fair, Broadbeach.

item.title: Boring Without You (BWU) guide: skincare made for combination skin
item.description: A pharmacist-reviewed guide to Boring Without You (BWU), the Australian brand made for combination skin: its cleanser, serum, gel moisturiser and multi-mask.

item.title: CeraVe guide: which cleanser and moisturiser suits your skin?
item.description: Which CeraVe cleanser and moisturiser suits your skin? A pharmacist-reviewed guide to ceramides, oily, acne-prone and eczema-prone skin, and CeraVe SPF 50.

item.title: La Roche-Posay guide: Effaclar, Cicaplast, Lipikar, Anthelios and more
item.description: Effaclar for oily skin, Toleriane for sensitive skin, Lipikar and Cicaplast for dry patches, Anthelios SPF50+ and the serums: La Roche-Posay explained.

item.title: Medicube guide: Zero Pore Pads, PDRN serum and how to use them
item.description: A pharmacist-reviewed guide to Medicube, the Korean skincare brand: Zero Pore Pads, PDRN Pink serum, collagen masks, kojic acid pads and how to use them.

item.title: The Ordinary guide: what to use for your skin, and what not to mix
item.description: Niacinamide, salicylic acid, retinal and more: which The Ordinary products suit oily, dry or acne-prone skin, what not to mix, and the Peeling Solution rules.

item.title: Vaccinations for China: what Australians need before they go
item.description: China needs no entry vaccines, but check measles, flu, hepatitis A and typhoid. Extra advice for family visits, altitude in Tibet and live animal markets.

item.title: Vaccinations for Fiji: what Australians need before they go
item.description: Fiji has no malaria and is rabies-free, but dengue and leptospirosis after floods are risks. The vaccines to check, from measles to typhoid, and food safety.

item.title: Vaccinations for India: what Australians need before they go
item.description: Most travellers to India need hepatitis A and typhoid vaccines. Why visiting family raises your risk, rabies and JE advice, and a fake rabies vaccine alert.

item.title: Why your pharmacist asks questions (and sometimes for ID)
item.description: How medicines are grouped in Australia, why pharmacists ask who it's for, why some cold and flu tablets need photo ID, and the rules on early repeats.

item.title: Vaccinations for Bali: what Australians need before they go
item.description: No vaccines are needed to enter Bali, but measles, hepatitis A and typhoid are worth having. When rabies and JE vaccines make sense, and avoiding Bali belly.

item.title: Ear piercing aftercare: how to look after a new piercing
item.description: How to clean a new ear piercing, how long it takes to heal, when you can change earrings or swim, and the signs of infection. From our Pacific Fair team.

item.title: Free vaccines at the pharmacy in Queensland: who's eligible in 2026
item.description: Which vaccines are free at a Queensland pharmacy in 2026: flu, COVID-19, RSV, shingles, pneumococcal, catch-ups and more, who qualifies and what changed.

item.title: Hangover remedies: what actually helps, and what doesn't
item.description: Big night in Broadbeach? What actually helps a hangover, what doesn't, which pain relief to choose, and the signs of alcohol poisoning and drink spiking.

item.title: Do you need vaccinations for Japan? What Australians should know
item.description: Most trips to Japan need no special vaccines, but check measles and flu, ask about Japanese encephalitis for rural stays, and know Japan's medicine rules.

item.title: Mosquitoes on the Gold Coast: Ross River virus and bite prevention
item.description: Ross River and Barmah Forest viruses are Queensland's most common mosquito-borne illnesses. Symptoms, when to see a GP, and how to avoid bites this summer.

item.title: Padel on the Gold Coast: health benefits and how to avoid injury
item.description: Padel is booming on the Gold Coast. Its health and social benefits, common injuries, sun safety on outdoor courts and a pharmacist's tips for staying on court.

item.title: Passport photo requirements: Australia and common visa sizes
item.description: Australian passport photo rules (35–40mm by 45–50mm, plain background, no glasses), guarantor endorsement, and photo sizes for US, UK, China and more.

item.title: Red, stinging eyes after swimming: causes and relief
item.description: Why your eyes go red after the pool or beach, how to soothe them, why you should never swim in contact lenses, and the warning signs that need a doctor.

item.title: Swimmer's ear: symptoms, treatment and how to prevent it
item.description: Swimmer's ear is an outer ear canal infection that's common in a Gold Coast summer. Symptoms, prevention, when you need a GP and how a pharmacist can help.

item.title: Vaccinations for Thailand and Vietnam: a pharmacist's guide
item.description: Hepatitis A for most trips, typhoid especially for Vietnam or street food, and when rabies and JE vaccines make sense. Start 6 to 8 weeks before you fly.

item.title: Vaccines for uni students: placements, colleges and catch-ups
item.description: Starting uni? Which vaccines health students need before clinical placements, why college students need meningococcal vaccines, and which catch-ups are free.

item.title: How to move your prescriptions to a new pharmacy
item.description: Moving scripts to a new pharmacy is free. How to bring across eScripts, your Active Script List, paper repeats and your PBS Safety Net record, step by step.

item.title: Christmas gift ideas for everyone on your list
item.description: Christmas gift ideas from Priceline Pacific Fair: fragrance, makeup, skincare, men’s grooming, electric toothbrushes and stocking fillers, with free gift help.

item.title: 60-day prescriptions: which medicines, who can get them and what you save
item.description: Two months' supply for one PBS co-payment: who can get a 60-day script, how to check if your medicine qualifies, and what it saves a general patient.

item.title: Can you drink alcohol while taking antibiotics?
item.description: Only a few antibiotics react badly with alcohol, and we label those boxes. Why drinking can still slow your recovery, and how to plan around party season.

item.title: Sun protection for babies: what's safe under 12 months
item.description: Queensland's UV Index is 3 or above all year, so babies need shade, clothing and hats. Why sunscreen waits until 6 months, and how to cover a pram safely.

item.title: How to choose the right sunscreen for Gold Coast conditions
item.description: A buyer's checklist for the best sunscreen on the Gold Coast: SPF50+, broad spectrum, water resistance, humid-weather textures, kids and makeup.

item.title: Paracetamol and ibuprofen for kids: doses, timing and safety
item.description: Dose by weight, not age: how often to give children's paracetamol and ibuprofen, the daily limits, who shouldn't have ibuprofen, and whether to give both.

item.title: Cold sores and the sun: triggers and what helps
item.description: Can the sun trigger a cold sore? Why UV sets them off, SPF lip balm for Gold Coast beach days, what to do at the first tingle and when to see a GP.

item.title: Contraception consultations with a Queensland pharmacist: how they work
item.description: How contraception consultations with a trained Queensland pharmacist work: who's eligible, what happens in the consult and when you'll see a GP. Pacific Fair.

item.title: Dry mouth: common causes (including medicines) and what helps
item.description: About 600 medicines can cause dry mouth, including antidepressants and antihistamines. Why it matters for your teeth, and what helps if a medicine is the cause.

item.title: Eczema in summer: keeping flare-ups under control
item.description: Eczema in summer myths vs facts: heat, sweat, pool and beach swimming, sunscreen for sensitive skin and when to see a GP, for humid Gold Coast weather.

item.title: Electric vs manual toothbrush: which is better?
item.description: A Cochrane review of 56 trials found powered brushes cut plaque and gingivitis more, but technique matters most. Who benefits and which features are worth it.

item.title: Fake tan: how to apply it, make it last, and why you still need SPF
item.description: Fake tan gives no UV protection, so you still need sunscreen daily in Queensland. How to prep, apply with a mitt without streaks, make it last and remove it.

item.title: Summer holiday first aid kit checklist (Gold Coast edition)
item.description: A first aid kit checklist for Gold Coast summer holidays: what to pack for the beach, pool, theme parks and road trips, plus keeping medicines cool.

item.title: Forgot your medicine on holiday? How to get it on the Gold Coast
item.description: Forgot medication on holiday? Step-by-step options for Gold Coast visitors from interstate and overseas, including eScripts and a GP inside our store.

item.title: Fragrance gift ideas from our beauty advisors
item.description: Fragrance gift ideas from our Pacific Fair beauty advisors: scent families, EDT vs EDP, testing tips and how Gold Coast heat and humidity change fragrance.

item.title: Fragrance and sensitive skin: allergies, sun reactions and wearing scent
item.description: Fragrance is the most common cause of contact dermatitis from cosmetics. Allergy or irritation, patch testing, fragrance-free vs unscented, and sun reactions.

item.title: Gastro in kids: how to keep them hydrated and when to worry
item.description: Small sips often, even if they're vomiting: using oral rehydration solution (frozen into ice blocks), signs of dehydration and Queensland childcare rules.

item.title: Are gel nails and UV nail lamps safe? UV, allergies and removal
item.description: Gel nails carry two risks: UV from the curing lamp and allergy to acrylates such as HEMA. How to reduce both, why DIY kits add risk, and safe removal.

item.title: Generic vs brand-name medicines: are they the same?
item.description: Generics have the same active ingredient in the same amount, checked by the TGA. Why the box looks different, what the PBS brand premium is and how to ask.

item.title: Hayfever on the Gold Coast: why our season is different
item.description: Our subtropical grasses flower through summer and autumn, so Gold Coast hayfever peaks later than down south. A local pollen calendar and ways to cut exposure.

item.title: Head lice: how to get rid of them (and stop them coming back)
item.description: Treat, then treat again: conditioner and a lice comb every 2 to 3 days, or a lotion repeated after 7 days. Why lice come back, the myths, and school rules.

item.title: Heat exhaustion vs heatstroke: symptoms, first aid, hydration
item.description: Heat exhaustion symptoms vs heatstroke, step-by-step first aid, when to call 000 and hydration tips for a humid Gold Coast summer, from our local pharmacy.

item.title: How to help an ageing parent manage their medicines
item.description: Visiting Mum or Dad over the holidays? How to help an elderly parent with medication: warning signs, medicines lists, packs, reviews and safe disposal.

item.title: How often should you clean makeup brushes and sponges?
item.description: Foundation brushes need washing every one or two uses, powder brushes every week or two. Step-by-step cleaning and drying, and when to replace your tools.

item.title: How to get rid of old medicines safely (free at the pharmacy)
item.description: Unwanted medicines go back to any pharmacy for free, safe disposal. What we accept at our Pacific Fair counter, where sharps go, and how to read expiry dates.

item.title: eScripts, Active Script Lists and scripts on file, explained
item.description: An eScript is a QR code token sent to your phone. How to use it at any pharmacy, when an Active Script List is easier, and what to do if you lose a token.

item.title: Magnesium supplements: which type, and what the evidence says
item.description: Citrate, chloride and lactate forms absorb better than magnesium oxide. The evidence for cramps and sleep, who runs low, and which medicines to space it from.

item.title: How to make perfume last longer in Gold Coast heat
item.description: Apply to moisturised skin on warm pulse points, let it dry without rubbing, and store it cool and dark: how to make scent last in Gold Coast heat and humidity.

item.title: Does makeup expire? How long mascara, foundation and lipstick last
item.description: Mascara lasts about three months once opened; powders keep longest. Reading the open-jar symbol, why old eye makeup is risky, and storing makeup in the heat.

item.title: Mineral vs chemical sunscreen: which is right for your skin?
item.description: Both types protect, Cancer Council says. How mineral and chemical filters differ, which suit sensitive or breakout-prone skin and kids, and nanoparticle safety.

item.title: Normal blood pressure: numbers explained (and when to act)
item.description: What's a normal blood pressure? Australian ranges in a simple chart, what readings like 120/84 mean, and where to get a free check at Pacific Fair, Broadbeach.

item.title: Can you take paracetamol and ibuprofen together?
item.description: Yes, most healthy adults can. How to time doses, the daily limit for each, how to avoid doubling up with cold and flu tablets, and who should skip ibuprofen.

item.title: PBS Safety Net 2026: thresholds, tracking and what you pay after
item.description: In 2026 the PBS Safety Net is $1,748.20 for general patients and $277.20 with a concession card. How to count family scripts, and what you pay after.

item.title: Pigmentation and melasma in Queensland: what helps
item.description: Most uneven skin tone in Queensland comes back to the sun. Sun spots vs melasma vs acne marks, why daily tinted SPF50+ helps, and which ingredients may help.

item.title: Postpartum hair loss: why it happens and when it stops
item.description: Shedding often starts two to three months after birth and usually settles on its own. Why it happens, what's normal, supplements, and when to see a GP.

item.title: Should you take a probiotic with antibiotics?
item.description: Some probiotic strains may reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhoea, but not every product has been studied. Timing, choosing a strain and who should avoid them.

item.title: Retinol for beginners: how to start without irritation
item.description: Start low and slow: two or three nights a week, a moisturiser after and SPF every morning. Irritation vs purging, what not to mix, and pregnancy advice.

item.title: Shingles vaccine: who can get it free and why it matters
item.description: The shingles vaccine is free under the NIP from 65, from 50 for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and for some immunocompromised adults.

item.title: Skincare for humid weather: a Gold Coast summer routine
item.description: Sticky Gold Coast summer? Skincare for humid weather: sweat, air-con, breakouts and a simple day and night routine for oily, dry and sensitive skin.

item.title: Skincare routine order: what goes on first (and what not to mix)
item.description: Cleanse, then go thinnest to thickest. Where sunscreen goes in the morning, why retinol and acids go on different nights, and niacinamide with vitamin C.

item.title: SPF30 vs SPF50+: does the number matter on the Gold Coast?
item.description: SPF30 filters about 96.7% of UVB and SPF50+ about 98.3%. Why Cancer Council still recommends 50+, what the label means, and why using enough matters more.

item.title: Does SPF in your foundation count? Sunscreen under makeup, done right
item.description: SPF in foundation isn't as effective as a primary sunscreen, UQ researchers say. How to layer sunscreen under makeup, reapply over it, and humid-day textures.

item.title: Supplements that can interact with your medicines
item.description: St John's wort with antidepressants and the pill, vitamin K with some blood thinners, minerals with some antibiotics: supplement interactions and staying safe.

item.title: Teeth whitening strips and kits: are they safe?
item.description: Home whitening kits in Australia are limited to lower peroxide strengths, but sensitivity and gum burns still happen. Who should see a dentist first.

item.title: Threadworms: how to treat the whole family and stop reinfection
item.description: Treat everyone in the house at once, even people without symptoms, and usually repeat in one to two weeks. The hygiene steps that stop eggs reinfecting you.

item.title: Travel health checklist: what to sort 6–8 weeks before you fly
item.description: Our travel health checklist counts down from 8 weeks to the day before you fly: vaccines, scripts, PBS rules and a travel kit, sorted at Pacific Fair.

item.title: Travel sickness on theme park rides, boats and road trips
item.description: Travel sickness tips for Gold Coast theme parks, whale-watching tours and winding hinterland drives, for kids and adults, plus when to see a GP.

item.title: Vitamin D on the Gold Coast: do you still need a supplement?
item.description: Most Gold Coast locals get enough vitamin D from everyday sun. Who still runs low, how to balance sun and skin cancer risk, testing, and supplement doses.

item.title: What can a pharmacist treat in Queensland without a GP?
item.description: Trained Queensland pharmacists can treat UTIs, offer contraception consultations and help with reflux, ear infections, school sores, eczema, acne and shingles.

item.title: Flu season in Queensland: when to get your flu shot
item.description: When to get your flu shot in Queensland before the winter peak, who may get it free, side effects and what to expect. Walk-in flu shots at Pacific Fair.

item.title: Whooping cough vaccine in pregnancy: what you need to know
item.description: Recommended in every pregnancy, ideally at 20 to 32 weeks, so antibodies reach your baby before birth. Whether it's free, and why partners and carers matter.

item.title: Acne treatment at the pharmacy: what actually helps
item.description: Acne treatment from the pharmacy: what helps, how long it takes and when to see a GP. Pharmacist tips on sunscreen and skincare for humid Gold Coast days.

item.title: Athlete’s foot treatment: how to clear it for good
item.description: Athlete's foot treatment: pharmacy antifungal options, how long to use them and when to see a GP. Tips for humid Gold Coast summers, pools and gym showers.

item.title: Bluebottle sting treatment: what to do (and what not to do)
item.description: Stung by a bluebottle on the Gold Coast? Step-by-step first aid from Australian guidelines, myths to ignore (vinegar, urine) and when to call 000.

item.title: Common cold remedies: myths, facts and what helps
item.description: Common cold remedies that ease symptoms, cold vs flu, why antibiotics don't help, and safe options for kids. Advice from our Pacific Fair pharmacists.

item.title: Constipation relief: a pharmacist’s checklist
item.description: Constipation relief that works: fibre, fluids, toilet position and laxative types explained, plus tips for Gold Coast holidays and when to see a GP.

item.title: Dandruff treatment: your questions answered
item.description: Dandruff treatment explained: causes, medicated shampoos, home tips and when to see a GP. Handy advice for Gold Coast swimmers who wash their hair often.

item.title: Dry skin remedies: a pharmacist’s checklist
item.description: Dry skin remedies that work: shower habits, choosing a moisturiser and when to see a GP. Tips for skin dried out by Gold Coast sun, salt water and air-con.

item.title: Haemorrhoids treatment: myths, facts and home care
item.description: Haemorrhoids treatment at home and from the pharmacy, why drinking water matters in Gold Coast heat, and when any bleeding means you should see a GP.

item.title: Headache relief: your questions answered
item.description: Headache relief explained: tension-type triggers like Gold Coast heat and dehydration, safe pain relief, medication-overuse headache and when to call 000.

item.title: Heartburn relief and GORD: what actually helps
item.description: Heartburn relief from our Broadbeach pharmacists: common triggers, eating and sleep tips, pharmacy reflux medicines, and when chest pain means call 000.

item.title: How to treat a cut or scrape: step-by-step first aid
item.description: How to treat a cut or scrape: stop bleeding, clean, cover and spot infection. Plus tetanus advice and red flags for Gold Coast beach and holiday injuries.

item.title: Migraine relief: what to do when an attack starts
item.description: Migraine relief step by step: spot the warning signs, act early, know your triggers like Gold Coast storms and glare, and when a headache means call 000.

item.title: Mouth ulcer treatment: home care and when to worry
item.description: Mouth ulcer treatment: saltwater rinses, soft foods (skip the salty beach chips), pharmacy gels, and when an ulcer needs a Gold Coast dentist or GP.

item.title: Nail fungus treatment: myths, facts and what works
item.description: Nail fungus treatment myths vs facts: pharmacy nail lacquers, when you need a GP and why it takes months. Foot tips for humid Gold Coast summers and pools.

item.title: Scabies treatment in Australia: your questions answered
item.description: Scabies treatment in Australia: pharmacy and GP options, treating your whole household, washing bedding, and advice for Gold Coast share houses.

item.title: Sprain vs strain: what’s the difference and what to do
item.description: Sprain vs strain explained, with RICE and No HARM first aid for ankles rolled on Gold Coast sand, plus the red flags that mean a GP visit or X-ray.

item.title: Sun safety on the Gold Coast: why UV is a year-round job
item.description: Gold Coast UV hits 3+ every day, even in winter. Simple sun safety for beach days, the school run and car parks, plus when to get a spot checked by a GP.

item.title: Sunburn treatment: what to do after too much sun
item.description: Sunburn treatment step by step: cool, soothe and protect burnt skin, and know when to see a GP. Pharmacist tips for Gold Coast beach days and holidays.

item.title: Trouble sleeping: tips from your local pharmacist
item.description: Trouble sleeping tips for hot, humid Gold Coast nights: routines, caffeine timing, when to see a GP and how our Pacific Fair pharmacists can help.
